subsystems.name: Light engine
subsystems.role: provides coherent red, green and blue light to form the hologram.

subsystems.name: Spatial light modulator
subsystems.role: encodes the holographic interference pattern onto the light wavefront.

subsystems.name: Hologram computation unit
subsystems.role: calculates the light pattern needed for each frame in real time.

subsystems.name: Optical relay and projection
subsystems.role: forms the wavefront in free space at the intended viewing zone.

subsystems.name: Eye tracking and view adaptation
subsystems.role: detects viewer positions and adjusts the hologram so each eye sees correct depth.

subsystems.name: Volumetric medium (optional)
subsystems.role: provides a physical volume where light scatters to form a visible 3D image.

buildSteps.title: Specify the viewing geometry
buildSteps.detail: Decide image size, depth range, viewing angle and number of simultaneous viewers. This sets the required modulator resolution and optical aperture.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate high-resolution phase modulators
buildSteps.detail: In a cleanroom, build a CMOS backplane with millions of pixel electrodes, then apply a liquid-crystal layer and alignment layers.

buildSteps.title: Implement the hologram generation software
buildSteps.detail: Write algorithms that compute phase patterns from 3D scene data, using GPU acceleration and techniques such as Fresnel diffraction or point-cloud methods.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the optical train
buildSteps.detail: Mount lasers, modulators and lenses on a rigid bench, align them to sub-micron precision, and calibrate wavefront aberrations.

buildSteps.title: Integrate real-time tracking
buildSteps.detail: Add cameras and infrared illumination, calibrate them to the optical system, and link tracking data to the hologram computation.

buildSteps.title: Test and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Measure resolution, depth accuracy, viewing angle, brightness and colour fidelity; reduce speckle and crosstalk by optimising algorithms and optics.

buildSteps.title: Package and control
buildSteps.detail: Enclose the system, manage heat from lasers and electronics, and build a user interface that converts standard 3D models into holographic frames.

prerequisites.why: current modulators have millions of pixels, but true holographic displays need hundreds of millions for wide viewing angles and large sizes.
demonstrated for simple scenes, but complex dynamic scenes at video rate require far more computing power.

prerequisites.tech: Coherent or partially coherent light sources
prerequisites.why: laser diodes and LEDs are widely available and compact.
used in AR/VR, but integrating with holographic displays requires very low latency and high accuracy.
fog, plasma and rotating screens have been demonstrated in labs, but they are bulky, dim or slow.

pathway.milestone: research prototypes show small, limited-colour floating images with narrow viewing angles
pathway.unlocks: understanding of optical and computational limits.

pathway.milestone: higher-resolution modulators and faster algorithms enable larger, full-colour images with wider viewing angles
pathway.unlocks: practical use in design review and medical imaging.

pathway.milestone: integration of eye tracking and multi-user support
pathway.unlocks: displays usable by several people at once without headsets.

pathway.milestone: consumer or professional displays with video-rate, full-colour, wide-angle 3D images
